session_title: Annual Roundup of 'Small Favors Done in Passing'

content.text: Fang Qing, thanks to you over the past year, we bought the right schoolbag for the child, and my wife has learned how to prepare meals, which has made things much easier. It seems like all I did was ask about sharing the cost of neutering in the fleet, and I haven’t really helped with much else.
How can you say I didn't help? The firsthand information you provided made my health reminders more down-to-earth. And regarding the bus route issue last time, your feedback was crucial.

Come to think of it, what you said reminds me of some small things. For example, you told me which brand of disinfectant has a mild smell, which is very practical. I recommended it to my colleagues in the fleet, and everyone responded quite well.

Yes, during that peak flu season, you shared my prevention infographic and asked about protection methods in the carriage, so I thought I should recommend something practical. You reminded me to pay attention to the stray dog at the station, which made me notice more details. Later, during the community disinfection event, I made a point of paying extra attention to the surrounding environment.
Well, small things add up. That time you shared the group-buy for apples, my wife was so happy. She said they were sweet and cheap, and it saved her a trip to the supermarket.
Haha, it's no trouble at all. The traffic updates you provide, like which roads are under construction or congested, often help me adjust my commute route and save a lot of time.
It seems we have quite a few of these 'little favors' to handle. How about organizing them and putting up a sticky note as a reminder?
Great idea! I have some sticky notes here; we can write it down. Wait a moment, I'll take a photo and send it to you.
Sent it over. This is what I just posted, some phrases aren't fully written yet, like 'providing routes...', which can be added now.
Got it, that's quite interesting. 'Reminder of disinfectant smell'—is that the brand I just mentioned? 'Share group-buy apples' is also on there. What is 'Little Knowledge'?
Regarding the little knowledge about carriage ventilation you asked earlier, I just mentioned it casually, and you remembered it.
I see. 'Mutual aid in small matters' is a good summary, it really captures the essence of our scattered help. I'll add 'providing route feedback,' just like you mentioned earlier.
Yes, and you helped gather information, like about the team training, which allowed me to prepare materials in advance and greatly improved efficiency.
Speaking of which, the health advice you gave me, like meal prep tips, my wife has really gotten the hang of it, and our family's diet is more balanced now.
Likewise. Your observations from the driver's perspective, such as passenger habits, have helped me optimize the health promotion content, making it more aligned with actual needs.
Upon reflection, these small gestures truly make life and work run more smoothly. Without any ulterior motives, it's simply about lending each other a hand, which feels quite heartwarming.
Yes, looking back on this year, we've become reliable supporters in each other's lives. This sense of human connection is more precious than anything.
Well, let's keep helping out like this in the future. By the way, if you need the fleet to assist with that community health activity you mentioned earlier, just let me know anytime.
Thank you, Chen Lu! I'll definitely reach out if I need anything. Let's stay in touch and support each other through both small and big matters.
Alright, it's settled then. See you later, and drive safely.
